items.title: Emile Barnes and Paul Barnes Interview, 1959-10-01
items.q: But anyway, we formed this band called Lawrence Murad and I. It was the original Diamond Band.

ctx.x: I know a lot of people bought those and they wouldn't even have a part for them in late years anymore.

Yeah, late years they cut it. They changed the orchestration. Orchestration used to be put up for shell and oboe and all that stuff as time went to change. But anyway, we formed this band called Lawrence Murad and I. It was the original Diamond Band. And we had Bush Hall on the trumpet. That's the time I'd taken a wife. We weren't making much money. And then I went with Kid René's band. That was up until 1922. And I went with Kid René's band. I wanted to get me, especially Simon Murad was in the band. So I quit…

items.title: Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1959-01-02
items.q: when I put up my own band with Bush Hall's name, Paul Barnes, my brother

ctx.x: But your brother John is the one that taught you? Yeah, my brother John. Did he just teach you by ear at first or did he try to teach you to read by the way? Well, no, he teach me by ear.

Mm-hmm. He teach me by ear. That's how I learned first. But I learned music long, long years after when I put up my own band with Bush Hall's name, Paul Barnes, my brother, Edward Moreira, bass violin, and my cousin Josiah Frazier on drums.
Oh, while we're talking about that, how are you related to Paul Barnes and Emil Barnes, of course. They're cousins too, aren't they?

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1969-06-16
items.q: And Lawrence, we got, we got, we made a band. And we called it the, the original Diamond Orchestra.

ctx.x: What was the first band you played in, around here? You know, the first organized band.
The first, the first organized band that I played in, was my own band. And Lawrence, we got, we got, we made a band. And we called it the, the original Diamond Orchestra.

items.title: Paul Barnes Interview, 1971-03-13
items.q: So Lawrence Marrera and Eddie Marrera, they came out playing music. See, from my mother's sister.

ctx.x: Well did your father encourage you all to play music? Or did he?

Well no he did not, because my father left home when I was about six years old. Oh you were that young. He never came back home anymore. So the fact is I just don't know where Millie picked it up at. But if Millie had picked up a trombone, then why not that be a trombone player? He picked up a trumpet, I did a trumpet player. Now the other brother was Reza-Mo, that was her oldest brother. And his children played music. Now he had, we call him Sam Frazier. Shuganu, nickname. Shuganu. He was a drum player. He was…

family. Oh yeah, I can see that easily.
